name: eps_tau
label: epsilon Tauri (Ain, K0 III red clump, Hyades)
sources: Boyajian et al. 2009, ApJ 691, 1243 (CHARA Classic, K' band): theta_LD = 2.733 +/- 0.031 mas (uniform disk 2.659; includes the van Belle et al. 1999 PTI point); earlier Mark III 2.671, NPOI 2.41, PTI 2.57
Anugu et al. 2026: radius 12.46 +/- 0.10 Rsun; Gaia DR3 parallax 22.3654 +/- 0.1721 mas -> 44.7 pc: 2R/d = 2.59 mas; the CHARA diameter is 5 % larger
Baines et al. 2025: T_eff 4880 +/- 67 K; Teng et al. 2023: log g 2.66; Arentoft et al. 2019: mass 2.458 +/- 0.073 Msun
Sato et al. 2007: V 3.53, red-clump giant with a planet; 2MASS H 1.314, K 1.31
SIMBAD: B V (Ducati 2002 / Oja 1993), H (2MASS), K (Ducati 2002)
notes: A northern red-clump calibrator for the ISI (hd360 and hd17652 are the southern ones); first null 84 m at 900 nm, 61 m at 650 nm.
Anchors are Vega magnitudes converted with the band table's Vega -> AB offsets (V +0.02, H +1.39, K +1.85); 900 and 900 nm fall inside the anchored range.

theta_LD is the CHARA K'-band limb-darkened diameter (2008 data); 2R/d from the Anugu et al. 2026 radius and the Gaia distance gives 2.59 mas, 5 % smaller. The radius used is derived from theta_LD and the distance.

The atmosphere block names the 5000 K dwarf as a STAND-IN: no NewEra model exists at log g 2.66; the Hyades campaigns bracket the giant between lte05000-4.50-0.0 (compact) and lte05000-0.00-0.0 (extended), with lte05000-4.50+0.5 for the metallicity (docs/hyades_ld.md).
assumptions: atmosphere.model (stand-in: a 5000 K dwarf, not a giant)
